# 046-numeric-formats — info

*Generated by `096` from the declarations in `046-numeric-formats.md`. Do not edit this page;
edit the blueprint and run the sweep again.*

**How numbers are written down** — phase 6.
Described by `606`.

## What it publishes

| symbol | unit | kind | value | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `b1` | bit | given | 1 bit | one bit. A width carries the unit so that a format's size can be added to a capacity; an exponent needs a pure number. Dividing by this is how a width becomes a count, and it is the only place in the project where a unit quantity is declared for that purpose |
| `w_weight` | bit | given | 4 bit | bits per weight index |
| `n_group` | 1 | given | 128 | weights sharing one expansion table and one scale |
| `w_scale` | bit | given | 16 bit | width of a group's scale |
| `w_act` | bit | given | 16 bit | activations in the residual stream |
| `w_operand` | bit | given | 8 bit | engine operands |
| `w_kv` | bit | given | 8 bit | key and value cache entries |
| `w_logit` | bit | given | 32 bit | logits, on face five only |
| `n_round_mode` | 1 | given | 1 | rounding modes the machine has. One, so that no conversion anywhere can differ between two implementations |
| `special_vals` | 1 | given | 0 | whether denormals, infinities and not-a-number are propagated. They are not; producing one raises a trap |
| `w_weight_eff` | bit | derived | 4.125 bit | bits per weight including the amortised scale, which is the number that decides how long a token takes |
| `f_scale_cost` | 1 | derived | 0.030303 | what the scale costs as a share of the weight read, which is the whole of open question F1 |
| `w_weight_8` | bit | derived | 8.125 bit | what eight-bit weights would cost, for the comparison |
| `speed_ratio` | 1 | derived | 1.9697 | how much faster four bits makes the machine than eight, which is the trade being made |
| `range_operand` | 1 | derived | 128 | largest magnitude an engine operand can carry |
| `n_lut_bits` | bit | derived | 256 bit | bits of expansion table one group carries, which the slice stores alongside the weights |

## What it consumes

| symbol | from | value | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `C_weights` | `078` | 36.3764 GB | the weights, resident, at the format in 046 |
| `n_lut_entry` | `045` | 16 | entries in the shared expansion table one group of weights indexes |
| `n_param` | `078` | 7.05482e+10 | the whole model |
| `w_acc` | `045` | 32 bit | accumulator width |

## What it asserts

| tag | relation | because |
|---|---|---|
| `C-046-1` | `2^(w_weight / b1) == n_lut_entry` | the index width and the table size must match exactly, which is trivially true and catches one being edited without the other |
| `C-046-2` | `w_weight_eff * n_param ~= C_weights` | bits per weight including the amortised scale, times the reference model's parameter count, must equal the resident weight size in 078. Two routes to the size of the thing this machine exists to hold |
| `C-046-3` | `speed_ratio > 1.5` | four bits must make the machine at least half again faster than eight, or the accuracy is being spent for too little |
| `C-046-4` | `w_acc > 2 * w_operand` | the accumulator must be wider than the product of two operands, which is the weakest possible overflow check and is here because 045's real one depends on 077 |
| `C-046-5` | `n_round_mode == 1` | one rounding mode. Asserted as a value, because a second one is the ordinary way bit-exactness between two implementations quietly stops holding |
| `C-046-6` | `special_vals == 0` | special values are refused rather than propagated. Asserted so that a blueprint assuming a not-a-number can flow through a layer fails outright |
| `C-046-7` | `w_kv <= w_act` | the cache is no wider than the activations it stores, since it is a compressed record of them |
